items.stem: Which three dimensions does the HDI measure?
items.answer: Health, education and standard of living
items.markingKey: Health, education and standard of living. Life expectancy, schooling and GNI per capita (PPP).

items.stem: Distinguish between the HDI and the IHDI.
items.answer: The HDI averages achievements in health, education and income; the IHDI discounts each dimension for inequality, showing the loss in human development due to unequal distribution.
items.markingKey: The HDI averages achievements in health, education and income; the IHDI discounts each dimension for inequality, showing the loss in human development due to unequal distribution. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why sustainable development requires maintaining natural capital.
items.answer: Depleting forests, fisheries, soils and the climate reduces future productive capacity and well-being, so present growth may be at the expense of future generations. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Depleting forests, fisheries, soils and the climate reduces future productive capacity and well-being, so present growth may be at the expense of future generations. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: With reference to progress on the SDGs, explain how it illustrates sustainable development goals.
items.answer: The UN's 2024 SDG report found that only about 17% of SDG targets were on track for 2030. Covid-19, conflict and climate shocks have slowed progress, showing that development can be reversed
items.markingKey: Context (The UN's 2024 SDG report found that only about 17% of SDG targets were on track for 2030.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Covid-19, conflict and climate shocks have slowed progress, showing that development can be reversed – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to sustainable development goals.

items.stem: UNDP data for Sundara: life expectancy 68 years; expected schooling 14 years; mean schooling 7 years; GNI per capita (2017 PPP $) 2,500. The health index is (LE − 20)/(85 − 20). Calculate the health index and the education index (the average of expected schooling/18 and mean schooling/15).
items.markingKey: HI = 0.738; EI = 0.622. [M1] for correct method/working; [A1] for both indices. Award [A1] only with correct units/notation where relevant.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against the view that the HDI is the most useful measure of development.
items.answer: The HDI is more useful than GNI per capita alone, but development should be assessed using a range of indicators, including the IHDI, MPI and GII.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: multidimensional; widely available and comparable; simple to interpret. Arguments against: ignores inequality (hence IHDI), gender (GII), environment; equal weights are arbitrary; ignores freedom, security and quality of education; data quality problems. Supported judgement: The HDI is more useful than GNI per capita alone, but development should be assessed using a range of indicators, including the IHDI, MPI and GII.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Gender Inequality Index (GII)"?
options: A UNDP composite index of a long and healthy life (life expectancy), knowledge (expected and mean years of schooling) and a decent standard of living (GNI per capita at PPP)
One of the nine concepts — scarcity, choice, efficiency, equity, economic well-being, sustainability, change, interdependence and intervention — used to frame IA commentaries
A UNDP index measuring gender inequality in reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation
The 17 goals adopted by all UN member states in 2015 for achievement by 2030, including ending poverty, zero hunger, quality education, gender equality and climate action
items.answer: A UNDP index measuring gender inequality in reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation
items.markingKey: C. "Gender Inequality Index (GII)" is a UNDP index measuring gender inequality in reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation.

items.stem: Distinguish between composite indicators and single indicators of development.
items.answer: Single indicators measure one aspect (e.g. GNI per capita, life expectancy); composite indicators such as the HDI combine several dimensions into one index.
items.markingKey: Single indicators measure one aspect (e.g. GNI per capita, life expectancy); composite indicators such as the HDI combine several dimensions into one index. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "A country with a high HDI must have low inequality." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The HDI uses national averages; the IHDI shows that high-HDI countries such as the USA lose a significant share of their HDI to inequality.
items.markingKey: The HDI uses national averages; the IHDI shows that high-HDI countries such as the USA lose a significant share of their HDI to inequality. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of a poverty trap?
options: High saving → high investment → high growth
Low income → low saving → low investment → low productivity → low income
items.answer: Low income → low saving → low investment → low productivity → low income
items.markingKey: C. A self-reinforcing cycle.

items.stem: Using electricity access in sub-Saharan Africa as an example, explain infrastructure as a barrier to development.
items.answer: The IEA estimates that about 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa lacked access to electricity in 2022. Without reliable power, firms cannot use modern machinery and children study less, limiting productivity and human capital

items.stem: With reference to Zambia's debt default in 2020, explain how it illustrates debt as a barrier to development.
items.answer: Zambia became the first African country to default during the pandemic in November 2020 and took until 2024 to agree a debt restructuring. Heavy debt service and the default crowded out spending on development
items.markingKey: Context (Zambia became the first African country to default during the pandemic in November 2020 and took until 2024 to agree a debt restructuring.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "Corruption is the most significant barrier to economic development."
items.answer: Corruption is a major barrier, but the most significant barrier varies by country; often several barriers reinforce each other.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: diverts public resources; deters investment; undermines trust and institutions. Arguments against: some fast-growing economies had corruption (e.g. China); geography, disease, conflict and debt also matter; poverty traps and lack of infrastructure are fundamental. Supported judgement: Corruption is a major barrier, but the most significant barrier varies by country; often several barriers reinforce each other.

items.answer: Export-led growth opens the economy and promotes industries that compete in world markets; import substitution protects domestic industries to replace imports, which often leads to inefficiency.

items.stem: Outline one way in which Zambia's debt default in 2020 shows debt as a barrier to development.
items.answer: Zambia became the first African country to default during the pandemic in November 2020 and took until 2024 to agree a debt restructuring. Heavy debt service and the default crowded out spending on development
items.markingKey: Context (Zambia became the first African country to default during the pandemic in November 2020 and took until 2024 to agree a debt restructuring.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Heavy debt service and the default crowded out spending on development – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to debt as a barrier to development.

items.stem: With reference to Botswana's diamond revenues, explain how it illustrates good governance as a development strategy.
items.answer: Botswana used diamond revenues, managed through a joint venture with De Beers and prudent fiscal rules, to fund education, health and infrastructure, becoming an upper-middle-income country. Strong institutions turned resource wealth into development, avoiding the resource curse
items.markingKey: Context (Botswana used diamond revenues, managed through a joint venture with De Beers and prudent fiscal rules, to fund education, health and infrastructure, becoming an upper-middle-income country.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Strong institutions turned resource wealth into development, avoiding the resource curse – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to good governance as a development strategy.

items.stem: Outline one way in which Cuba and Costa Rica shows the difference between growth and development.
items.answer: Cuba and Costa Rica have life expectancies close to those of the USA despite much lower GNI per capita. Investment in primary health care and education achieved high human development at modest income levels
items.markingKey: Context (Cuba and Costa Rica have life expectancies close to those of the USA despite much lower GNI per capita.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Investment in primary health care and education achieved high human development at modest income levels – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the difference between growth and development.

items.stem: A student claims that a good IA commentary should summarise the whole article in detail. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Description earns few marks; the commentary should select the relevant issue, apply theory and diagrams, and evaluate, quoting the article only as evidence.
items.markingKey: Description earns few marks; the commentary should select the relevant issue, apply theory and diagrams, and evaluate, quoting the article only as evidence. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of the view that corruption is the most significant barrier to economic development.
items.answer: Corruption is a major barrier, but the most significant barrier varies by country; often several barriers reinforce each other.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: diverts public resources; deters investment; undermines trust and institutions. Arguments against: some fast-growing economies had corruption (e.g. China); geography, disease, conflict and debt also matter; poverty traps and lack of infrastructure are fundamental. Supported judgement: Corruption is a major barrier, but the most significant barrier varies by country; often several barriers reinforce each other.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim that foreign direct investment is the most effective strategy for promoting economic development.
items.answer: FDI can be powerful (China, Vietnam, Ireland) but its benefits depend on absorptive capacity, linkages and governance; it works best as part of a broader strategy.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: capital, technology and skills transfer; jobs and export earnings; tax revenue. Arguments against: profit repatriation and tax avoidance; enclave production with few linkages; environmental and labour exploitation; requires good infrastructure and institutions first. Supported judgement: FDI can be powerful (China, Vietnam, Ireland) but its benefits depend on absorptive capacity, linkages and governance; it works best as part of a broader strategy. Level 1 (1-3) little understanding.

items.stem:

Qatar's GNI per capita ranks among the highest in the world, but its HDI rank is noticeably lower than its GNI rank.

Cuba and Costa Rica have life expectancies close to those of the USA despite much lower GNI per capita.

Using information from the extract and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that the HDI is the most useful measure of development.
items.answer: The HDI is more useful than GNI per capita alone, but development should be assessed using a range of indicators, including the IHDI, MPI and GII.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: multidimensional; widely available and comparable; simple to interpret. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "informal economy"?
options: Transparent, accountable and effective government, with the rule of law, low corruption and protection of property rights
A UNDP composite index of a long and healthy life (life expectancy), knowledge (expected and mean years of schooling) and a decent standard of living (GNI per capita at PPP)
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs (Brundtland Report, 1987)
Economic activities that are not registered, regulated or taxed by the government
items.answer: Economic activities that are not registered, regulated or taxed by the government
items.markingKey: D. "informal economy" is economic activities that are not registered, regulated or taxed by the government.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Long-term investment by multinational corporations in productive assets in another country"?
items.answer: foreign direct investment (FDI)
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of foreign direct investment (FDI).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A UNDP index measuring gender inequality in reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation"?
items.answer: Gender Inequality Index (GII)
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of Gender Inequality Index (GII).

items.stem: Briefly explain why a relevant diagram must be explained, not only drawn, in an IA commentary.
items.answer: Marks for diagrams require that the diagram is accurate, labelled and explicitly linked to the article's situation; an unexplained diagram does not demonstrate application.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Marks for diagrams require that the diagram is accurate, labelled and explicitly linked to the article's situation; an unexplained diagram does not demonstrate application. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between political and social barriers and economic barriers to development.
items.answer: Economic barriers include poverty traps, poor infrastructure, low human capital, debt and commodity dependence; political and social barriers include corruption, weak institutions, conflict, gender inequality and lack of property rights.
items.markingKey: Economic barriers include poverty traps, poor infrastructure, low human capital, debt and commodity dependence; political and social barriers include corruption, weak institutions, conflict, gender inequality and lack of property rights. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between import substitution and export-led growth.
items.answer: Export-led growth opens the economy and promotes industries that compete in world markets; import substitution protects domestic industries to replace imports, which often leads to inefficiency.
items.markingKey: Export-led growth opens the economy and promotes industries that compete in world markets; import substitution protects domestic industries to replace imports, which often leads to inefficiency. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between the IHDI and the HDI.
items.answer: The HDI averages achievements in health, education and income; the IHDI discounts each dimension for inequality, showing the loss in human development due to unequal distribution.
items.markingKey: The HDI averages achievements in health, education and income; the IHDI discounts each dimension for inequality, showing the loss in human development due to unequal distribution. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between application in a commentary and evaluation in a commentary.
items.answer: Application links theory and diagrams to the specific facts of the article; evaluation weighs consequences, stakeholders, assumptions and priorities to reach a supported judgement.
items.markingKey: Application links theory and diagrams to the specific facts of the article; evaluation weighs consequences, stakeholders, assumptions and priorities to reach a supported judgement. items.stem: With reference to M-Pesa in Kenya, explain how it illustrates financial inclusion as a development strategy.
items.answer: A 2016 study by Suri and Jack estimated that access to M-Pesa lifted about 2% of Kenyan households out of extreme poverty. Mobile money lowered the cost of transfers and saving, helping households manage risk and move into business
items.markingKey: Context (A 2016 study by Suri and Jack estimated that access to M-Pesa lifted about 2% of Kenyan households out of extreme poverty.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Outline one way in which the Gulf states and the HDI shows composite indicators of development.
items.answer: Qatar's GNI per capita ranks among the highest in the world, but its HDI rank is noticeably lower than its GNI rank. Very high income has not been matched by equally high education outcomes, so the HDI gives a broader picture than income alone
items.markingKey: Context (Qatar's GNI per capita ranks among the highest in the world, but its HDI rank is noticeably lower than its GNI rank.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Briefly describe a news article on new tariffs on steel imports and explain what it reveals about how to apply the key concept of intervention in an IA.
items.answer: An article describes a government imposing a 25% tariff on steel imports to protect domestic producers. The commentary would use a tariff diagram to identify welfare effects and evaluate impacts on consumers, steel users, producers and trading partners
items.markingKey: Context (An article describes a government imposing a 25% tariff on steel imports to protect domestic producers.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Outline one way in which the Democratic Republic of the Congo shows the resource curse and weak institutions.
items.answer: The DRC has vast mineral wealth (including about 70% of world cobalt output), yet over 60% of its population lives in extreme poverty. Conflict, corruption and weak governance prevent resource revenues from funding development
items.markingKey: Context (The DRC has vast mineral wealth (including about 70% of world cobalt output), yet over 60% of its population lives in extreme poverty.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Conflict, corruption and weak governance prevent resource revenues from funding development – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the resource curse and weak institutions.

items.stem: Lars writes: "FDI always benefits the host country." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: MNCs may repatriate profits, use transfer pricing to avoid tax, create few local linkages, exploit lax labour or environmental standards, or crowd out local firms.
items.markingKey: MNCs may repatriate profits, use transfer pricing to avoid tax, create few local linkages, exploit lax labour or environmental standards, or crowd out local firms. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: UNDP data for Pacifica: life expectancy 76 years; expected schooling 12 years; mean schooling 13 years; GNI per capita (2017 PPP $) 25,000. The health index is (LE − 20)/(85 − 20). items.markingKey: HI = 0.862; EI = 0.767. [M1] for correct method/working; [A1] for both indices. Award [A1] only with correct units/notation where relevant.
